# Closure and Escalation Notes

**Deception - Service Ticket Requested for a Honey SPN Account** · `T1558.003_honey_spn_ticket_request` · [T1558.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1558/003/)

Fill in only what you checked. A confirmed attack is never closed from the queue: send the escalation note instead.

## Benign Positive

The rule fired on real activity that is expected and authorized.

```text
Alert:        T1558.003_honey_spn_ticket_request for <host> at <time, UTC>
Observed:     EventID=<value>  ServiceName=<value>
Checked:      1. Confirm the service account is a decoy in deceive/decoys.yml and that no Active Directory assessment was declared for the time -> <result>
              2. Resolve IpAddress to the requesting host and identify the requesting account (TargetUserName) -> <result>
              3. Count the distinct SPNs that host requested in the same ten minutes - the decoy's ticket is usually one of many -> <result>
Benign:       <which known source below> - confirmed by <change record, owner or ticket>
Disposition:  Benign Positive
Tuning:       none | declared_assessment_host (proposed)
```

Known benign sources for this detection:
- A vulnerability scanner or Active Directory assessment tool that requests a ticket for every SPN it finds

Never tune:
- Never filter by encryption type: AES requests for the decoy are the gap this rule exists to close.
- Never filter loopback or domain controller sources: a roasting tool run on a domain controller still asks for the decoy.
- Never drop the decoy from the rule without removing it from deceive/decoys.yml; rasd deceive --check fails on the difference.

Escalate when any of these holds:
1. The requesting host is a workstation
2. Several distinct SPNs were requested from the host in minutes (Kerberoasting in progress)
3. The decoy's ticket was requested with RC4 while the account allows AES (a deliberate downgrade)

Risk conditions: outside business hours +10 · user is privileged +5 · approved admin activity -40.

Containment options, after the evidence above is preserved:
1. Rotate the passwords of the real service accounts requested in the same burst
2. Isolate the requesting host
3. Keep the decoy; review its lure and record the touch in the deception log
